The `<deq-icon>` custom element for any page or framework.

```html
<script type="module">
  import "@0xdolan/deq-elements/define";
</script>
<deq-icon name="roj-half-sun" size="32" stroke-width="1.5"></deq-icon>
```

Source: [`packages/elements`](../../packages/elements/). Install with `npm install @0xdolan/deq-elements`.

## Functions

### `defineDeqElements`

```ts
function defineDeqElements(tag?: string): void
```

Register `<deq-icon>` (or another tag name). Safe to call more than once and on servers,
where it does nothing.

### `drawIcon`

```ts
function drawIcon(doc: Document, icon: DeqIcon, options?: IconOptions): SVGSVGElement
```

Build the `<svg>` element for `icon` with DOM calls (no HTML parsing).

## Classes

### `DeqIconElement`

```ts
class DeqIconElement
```

`<deq-icon name="roj-half-sun">`: draws a Deq icon inline (light DOM, so CSS `color`
and selectors work). Attributes: `name`, `size`, `color`, `stroke-width`,
`absolute-stroke-width` and `label` (the accessible title; `label=""` marks the icon
decorative). Set the `icon` property to draw custom icon data instead of `name`.

- `#icon: DeqIcon | undefined`
- `icon: DeqIcon | undefined`: Custom icon data; takes precedence over the `name` attribute.
- `connectedCallback: () => void`
- `attributeChangedCallback: () => void`
- `options: () => IconOptions`: The icon options from the attributes.
- `update: () => void`: Redraw the icon now. Lifecycle callbacks redraw automatically and leave the element empty for an unknown name or invalid attributes; this method throws instead.
- `#draw: () => void`
